shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures fell for a fifth straight session on Monday and hit its lowest point in more than two months as dry Midwest weather boosted harvest progress while forecasts called for continued good weather through the end of the week.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures fell for a fifth straight session on Monday and hit its lowest point in more than two months as dry Midwest weather boosted harvest progress while forecasts called for continued good weather through the end of the week.

The US Department of Agriculture is due to update its weekly crop progress estimates later on Monday. Analysts polled by Reuters, on average, expect the agency to report that US farmers have harvested 49% of their corn crop as of Sunday.

The USDA said 672,475 metric tons of US corn was inspected for export in the week ended October 15, down from 1,313,733 tons a week earlier and well below trade estimates that ranged from 1.1 million to 1.35 million tons.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) settled 7-1/4 cents lower at $4.67 a bushel.
